nonclaims: syntactic movement similarity is not strategic equivalence
small tied set (31 pairs, 22 signature classes)
no strength, utility or human-price claim

post_hoc_exactness.note: added after the pre-registered set-Jaccard run; descriptive only, no decision attached
post_hoc_exactness.interpretation: set Jaccard 1.0 means no move token is unique to either side; it does not imply identical multiplicity or identical stored signature
post_hoc_exactness.degenerate_threshold: reference p90 is 1.0 because more than 10% of reference pairs also share a token set, so the pre-written 90th-percentile comparison is satisfied but not sharp; the reference median 0.727 is the informative contrast

post_hoc_robustness.note: added after the pre-registered run; descriptive only, no new decision

multiset_jaccard_pooled.direction: same as the pre-registered set metric

post_hoc_robustness.caveat: near-equal raw scores already co-occur with similar movement signatures among the equal-score pairs, so benign_concentration describes the near-collision population rather than isolating a tie-specific bias; the distinct-score escaped comparison has only five pairs

post_hoc_matched_reference.note: added after the pre-registered run; descriptive only, no new decision
post_hoc_matched_reference.matching_rule: reference pair is matched when its unordered pair of token-set sizes equals the size pair of a tied pair; tied size pairs are 8v8, 8v9, 9v9, 9v10
post_hoc_matched_reference.fisher_note: tied pairs versus matched reference pairs that are not tied; shared types and rules make this descriptive, not an independent-sample test

pair_size.definition: unordered pair of distinct-token counts (token-set sizes)
